QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_3

question.text: Lotus AIF is a Category III scheme with INR 300 crore of investible funds. The portfolio manager, Mr. Rohan Deshmukh, wants to take a concentrated long position in a single listed mid-cap stock. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the MAXIMUM rupee exposure this scheme can take in that single investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category III AIFs, Regulation 15 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations caps exposure in a single investee company at 10% of investible funds. 10% of INR 300 crore = INR 30 crore. Cat I and Cat II AIFs have a higher 25% cap; Cat III has the tighter 10% limit precisely because of its leveraged/traded portfolio nature. The Trap: INR 75 crore (25%) is the Cat I/II limit — a tempting wrong answer if the candidate forgets Cat III has a stricter cap. INR 15 crore (5%) and INR 100 crore (33%) are fabricated thresholds. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B Distributor exam tests the same 10% Cat III cap; XXI-B PM exam has a 25% single-security cap for PMS schemes. XIX-C Manager must operationalise this through pre-trade compliance checks in the order management system. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build your OMS hard-block at 9.5% of investible funds, not 10% — leaves a buffer for mark-to-market drift that might otherwise push a compliant trade over the line intraday and trigger a Regulation 15 breach.
